---
title: Course framework
---

## Course direction

The course combines computational economic methods with practical research workflows. Lectures move through the core methods earlier, leaving a closing block for recent computational literature using machine-learning tools. Labs develop students' use of LLM agents for research, alongside Git and other regular tools. Python supports the work; teaching Python syntax is not the main lab objective.

## Topic decks and weekly sessions

The schedule is organized by week, while slides are organized by topic. A topic may occupy part of a week or continue across several weeks. The proposed allocation below is a planning frame, not finalized pacing. Weeks 11–13 are provisional literature slots; papers and readings have not been chosen.

The old standalone introduction to computational concepts is retired. Selected numerical ideas may be integrated into later lectures when they become relevant; this integration is still to be planned.

Week 1 has two lecture components: a **Course Introduction** placeholder and the topic-based **Introduction to Markov Decision Processes** deck moved from the previous Week 2. Week 10 provides space for synthesis or slower topic pacing. Exact allocations for Weeks 2–13 remain open for discussion.

## Weekly homework

Each week has a reading component and an exercise component. Paper selection, reading questions, exercise tasks, workload, submission arrangements, and due dates are placeholders. Nothing is assigned by a placeholder.

## Assessment

The existing replication-project policy remains in force pending a separate assessment decision: the project accounts for 100% of the grade; teams of 2–3 replicate as many papers as there are members. Adding homework placeholders does not assign new grading weights.

See the [project guide](project.qmd) and [literature framework](references.qmd).
